drivingQuestion: Which places have the status of בתי החצרים?
outcomeNote: A mishna stating a definition; no dispute and no argument within the unit.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ וְאֵלּוּ הֵן בָּתֵּי הַחֲצֵרִים — שְׁנֵי חֲצֵרִים שֶׁל שְׁנֵי בָתִּים, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמּוּקֶּפֶת חוֹמָה מִימוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן, הֲרֵי הֵן כְּבָתֵּי חֲצֵרִים.
segments.en: «MISHNA» «And these are the houses of the» unwalled «courtyards» whose halakha was taught in the previous mishna: Any city in which there are «two courtyards» each containing «two houses, although it is surrounded by a wall from the era of Joshua, son of Nun, their» halakhic status «is like that of the houses of» the unwalled «courtyards.»

moves.summary: defines the term בתי החצרים whose law the previous mishna stated
moves.about: defines what counts as 'houses of the unwalled courtyards', the term whose law the previous mishna stated: two courtyards of two houses each

moves.cueHe: אף על פי שמוקפת חומה מימות יהושע בן נון
moves.summary: the status holds even for a town walled since Joshua's day
moves.about: extends the category: a town with only two courtyards of two houses each counts as unwalled courtyards even if it has been walled since the days of Joshua son of Nun

edges.cueHe: ואלו הן בתי החצרים — שני חצרים של שני בתים
edges.about: defines what counts as 'houses of the unwalled courtyards', the term whose law the previous mishna stated: two courtyards of two houses each

edges.cueHe: אף על פי שמוקפת חומה מימות יהושע בן נון, הרי הן כבתי חצרים
edges.about: extends the category: a town with only two courtyards of two houses each counts as unwalled courtyards even if it has been walled since the days of Joshua son of Nun
